intro: Owner direction (2026-09-11): remove the Future-scope toggle, give every top icon a border and a word, indent the accordion bodies, re-audit, and build the research features 01 02 04 07 10 11.

The Future-scope switch is gone and the four features it gated are simply the product now. Every top-bar and builder-header icon is a bordered button with a label. Section bodies are indented 44 px to the title.

Each feature below follows its design-office verdict (references/research/NN-*/05-directions.html). Prototype links open at the start of the journey (?focus=<id>). Copy is proposed, not approved — the sign-off list is under each feature.

The NG token pass (Phase 1 of the revamp) is still ahead: these screens carry the Studio X look. One token was fixed on the way: --muted-foreground now clears AA, which removed most of the Phase-0 axe nodes.

Second pass, same evening: seven owner notes on the first delivery — strip removed, ghost More, NG-style header controls, a better test rail, Figma overlaps fixed, contrast, and a where-it-lives table (below) — plus three follow-ups from screenshots: one header line, side-by-side architecture cards, one primary CTA per fold.

Third and fourth pass (2026-09-12): ten owner notes on the chrome (Run test scenarios as a header door, full-height rail, Undo to live, Callers hear as a field, hosting region as label + value, red End test, no em dashes anywhere in copy) and three on the models fold (voice selection in the TTS config, + Add backup beside every vendor, credentials as a switch modelled on the NG console). Then a presence check of all six features on production: every marker matched.

Fifth pass (2026-09-12, owner IA notes): five surfaces had drifted into new designs of things that already had a home. Backup providers were a section of their own plus an inline select with no key; recommended voices were a list above the voice table; a Browse voices button duplicated the voice field; the runs empty state was centered while every other empty state is a left-aligned row; the builder header scrolled away while everything under it stuck. Each is now a state of the surface that already renders that kind of thing. The rule is recorded: things that belong together live together and look the same, and a default Agora handles needs no control.

Sixth pass (2026-09-15): twenty owner notes on the models sheet, the Opening section, the deployment flow and the copy. A backup is now a chain, not one pick: each link carries its own vendor, model, credential and on/off switch, because the owner's question was "what about the keys for the backup?" and a backup without a key is not a backup. Prompt & knowledge splits into three labelled rows. Batch calling gets its contact list at the point of decision. And the builder now carries a KPI strategy: a north star, a 180-second time budget with parts, three guardrails with owners, and eleven assumptions stated with numbers so they can be refuted.

Seventh pass (2026-09-15, same day): twenty-three more owner notes, and one of them sent me to Agora's own pricing docs. The rate is a flat $0.10 per agent-minute and the docs say it is the same with your own key, so the slider's Lowest-Cost end was measuring a number that never moves. The axis is now speed against capability with two badges, one that changes and one that does not. Advanced settings became a single panel with a contents list instead of four hiding places. Credentials are made inside the builder. Go live stopped asking for things Deployment already collected.

Eighth pass: the owner caught a sentence of mine arguing with the design inside the product, and the control that made me write it. A first-time reader never saw a cost axis, so answering "not money" was noise. The slider is gone; three named options replace it. Then the same class of copy came out of 27 other strings, and a lint now catches it. Finally, modals were broken at the primitive: three CSS bugs in Dialog, AlertDialog and Sheet that affected every one of them.

rationale: A switch that reveals unbuilt features in the product bar confuses reviewers (Phase 0 finding N4); now that the roadmap features are being built, they are shown.
Icon-only ghosts fail recognition over recall on a header with eight controls (A7); border + word costs 60 px and removes the guesswork.
44 px = padding + chevron + gap, so the body aligns with the title text — nested by geometry, not by a box.

Second pass (owner feedback, 2026-09-11 evening): the Start · Builder · All agents strip is gone (the breadcrumb carries location); More is a ghost button; Help · Notifications · Composer follow the NG console shell — 28 px ghost icon controls with a faint border and tint, the word in the tooltip and the accessible name, the real unread count on the bell.

Selected states: every toggle group and tab shares one rule — the chosen option is an ink-tinted chip with an ink border and semibold text (toggles) or a card with a 3:1 ring (tabs); the unchosen one is outlined on border-stroke. A first version used the primary fill and read as a CTA in dark mode, so it was replaced.
One primary per fold: Deploy owns the filled button; Generate scenarios and Add case in the test rail are outline.
The test rail's two tests are named by what you do — Scenarios (with its count) and Voice call — with a cross-link from the call to the scenarios; section 4 and the preflight say scenarios too.
The three builder columns share one 56 px header line (rail: n of 5 done · Collapse all; section header; test rail header). Model Architecture cards sit side by side.

Third pass (owner notes, 2026-09-12): the scenario suite left the rail's tab strip and became a header door, Run test scenarios, beside Custom config and Voice call; the open door reads as pressed. The rail is the viewport height so its border reaches the bottom. Reset to live is now Undo to live. Callers hear is a read-only field like Greeting, with Hear the opening on the same line and no new behaviour. Hosting region options carry their name only. End test, Delete and Remove use the destructive variant (a tint of red).

Copy rule, standing: no em dash in user-facing text. Every one was rewritten: label pairs use a middot, sentence elaborations a period or colon. The failure, judge and hosting hints now read as sentences.

Fifth pass (owner, 2026-09-12): the builder header (name, status, id, actions) is sticky under the app bar at all times; the rail, section headers and test rail stick under it, so the three columns keep one continuous line while scrolling.
The runs empty state was a centered block; every other empty state in the builder is a left-aligned bordered row with the door on the right. It now uses that row. Same thing, same look.

Sixth pass (owner, 2026-09-15): the manual door moved directly under the stack recap, so choosing a preset and building your own are neighbouring choices. Prompt & knowledge became three labelled rows with hairlines between them, because a system prompt, an opening and a failure message are three decisions and they had been reading as one list under a floating Opening title.

Caller-first used to grey out four controls and put explanatory prose inside a disabled input. It now hides them and says one sentence. Lines the agent speaks are set in quotes and italics wherever they appear, so what the caller hears is never confusable with the interface's own words.

Copy struck on the owner's instruction: the end-to-end latency note, the all-in explainer, the slider warning, the stop-bundle hint and the deployment blurb. Row titles are verbs in sentence case, and the label column balances its lines so no title ends on a single orphan word.

Deployment: picking Batch used to change nothing on screen. It now shows the caller ID and the contact list with its table open, and the rail carries a Contact list door while Batch is the chosen type. Go live keeps one name instead of renaming itself after the channel.

Seventh pass (owner, 2026-09-15): four advanced-settings doors became one panel with a contents list naming what each group holds, so nothing depends on remembering which sheet hid what. Conversation history and the raw config JSON moved there from the model expander; the silence rule moved there from the Opening section, where it had been sitting as a stray recap line.

The AI-disclosure sentence is a field like the greeting, and it carries what the pinned region actually requires with a link to the primary source: EU AI Act Article 50, Korea's AI Framework Act Article 31, Utah 13-77-104, MeitY's IT Rules FAQ, Japan's AI Promotion Act. It says plainly that the region is where the agent runs and the binding rule is where the caller is. Outbound adds the FCC's 2024 ruling that an AI voice is an artificial voice under the TCPA.

Go live lost the campaign-runs card, its roll-up, its status filter and its second caller-ID picker. The contact list and the number were chosen in Deployment, so it asks one thing: when to start. The deploy summary lost its card and gained the size of the batch.
Every string that talked about the prototype instead of the product is gone: no wireframe estimates, no simulated previews, no parenthetical annotations in the transcript.

Eighth pass (owner, 2026-09-15): "Every stop costs the same $0.10 a minute. The slider trades how fast the agent answers against how much it can handle, not money" was copy defending a decision. Only someone who saw the cost axis would need the words "not money". It is gone, and so is the slider: with price constant there was one real axis, and a dial with nothing to dial is the wrong control. Three options that say what they are for, each carrying its own answer time.

The same class of writing came out of 27 more strings that named the prototype rather than the product, and out of the disclosure block, the advanced panel's subtitle and the pre-flight description. CLAUDE.md now carries a copy gate with four tests, and scripts/copy-lint.mjs checks the mechanical half. It found those 27 on its first run.

Modals were broken at the primitive, which is why they were all broken. Dialog, AlertDialog and Sheet are CSS grids, and a grid child defaults to min-width auto, so any long value pushed through the panel edge instead of wrapping. Nothing bounded their height, so a tall dialog ran off the viewport with its own buttons out of reach. AlertDialog had no inset, so it touched the screen edges. Then the two the screenshots caught: the pre-flight's label column was narrower than the word DEPLOYMENT, and every row of the template diff was a flex with no minimum-width reset.

features.name: Greeting, filler & disclaimer
features.jtbd: The first seconds and the pauses feel natural — and compliant.

after.caption: After (seventh pass): a key is made in the builder, not on another page

marks.name: Keys are made without leaving the builder
marks.why: Create credential used to navigate to another page, which throws away the draft's React state. It is a dialog now. Only the last four characters are kept, which is all the picker ever shows.

rationale: Managed is cheaper than BYO and includes vendor usage, so Agora can own the backup pool for managed components; a BYO component asks for a second key.
Pinning a hosting region costs failover — 'no eligible backup in Europe' is a real state with two real fixes (unpin, add a key).
The public agent API has no fallback field (Engine P1 · Nov): the pool is a draft field, the button says so.

Fourth pass (owner, 2026-09-12): + Add backup sits beside each vendor field in Configure models manually. It opens a Backup vendor select with the primary vendor listed but disabled and ineligible vendors saying why; the pick writes the same draft the Backup providers row recaps, so there is one truth.

Credentials are a switch modelled on the NG console's credential select (src/components/console/studio-resource-select.tsx): off is Agora Managed Key with the shield and Included, no key to add; on is a select of saved credentials with No credential selected and Create credential. A BYO-only vendor keeps the switch on and disabled. The earlier saved-credential placeholder name was wrong and is gone.
Same-day fix (bfb4406): the inline component existed but was never mounted in the slot rows, so the first production check found no + Add backup. The shots above are from the fixed deploy.

Fifth pass (owner IA, 2026-09-12): the separate Backup providers section and the inline + Add backup are gone. A backup belongs to the model it protects, so it is set in that model's Configure sheet after the vendor, its credential and the model: Backup vendor (primary listed but disabled, ineligible vendors say why, No backup is a choice) and the backup's own credential, the same CredentialField as the primary. Agora's pool (AssemblyAI, Cartesia) and resold vendors run on Agora Managed Key; any other backup needs one of your saved credentials, and until then the recap says needs your {vendor} key. That answers the owner's question: what about the keys for the backup?

A default, managed Agora stack shows no backup control at all. One sentence in the cost card says Agora switches to its backup and nothing needs setting up. Backup UI appears only once you configure models manually, where the right panel already owns configuration, sequence and keys.

Why it drifted: the 07 verdict said one row, on by default, and I drew that row as a new section instead of extending the sheet that already held vendor and credential. The rule now: extend the existing surface, never add a sibling one. Test failover waits for the Engine failover contract (Nov) and is no longer a dead button on screen.

Sixth pass (owner, 2026-09-15): "what about the keys for the backup? Hence this will NOT work." A backup is now a chain, not a single pick. Vendor and model sit on one row, the credential under it, and each backup repeats that anatomy with its own on/off switch. Add backup appends the next; the switch takes one out of the chain without losing its key.
The Engine tries them in order. A backup whose vendor is not in Agora's pool asks for one of your saved credentials and is skipped until it has one, which the recap line says out loud.

Seventh pass: the credential control is a checkbox, not another switch, because each backup already carries one. Create credential opens a dialog in the builder; it used to navigate away, which throws the draft's React state away. Only the last four characters of a key are kept, which is all the picker ever shows. Dropped "Included, no key to add" and "on top of Agora's rate".
Custom model ID is named for what it is and now reaches the backups too. The recap under each model row says "Backup: vendor, model" and nothing else.
copy: Backup · If {vendor} is slow, down or blocked in your region, the call continues on the backup. Switching is never silent: every switch shows in the session log.
